subject: Post-demo: hosting path probe & latency/throughput clarifications
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@streamlinepay.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: hosting path probe & latency/throughput clarifications

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and a few targeted questions so we can size a pilot that demonstrates both latency and cost tradeoffs.

Recap of your requirements from the call:
- Checkout flow (real-time fraud + payment authorization): P95 <= 80ms target, peak concurrent requests ~600 (burstable to 900).
- Account summary / recommendations: can tolerate P95 up to 150ms, bulk/batch-friendly.
- Expected sustained QPS during peak: ~1,200 requests/min across endpoints (rough distribution noted below).
- Data sensitivity: payment tokens/partial PII — preference for isolation but the team is okay discussing managed solutions if we can meet audit controls.

Questions for clarification (short answers will help us pick Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):
1) For the checkout endpoint, is the 80ms P95 an absolute SLA window, or a preferred goal for user experience?
2) Can you share a simple RPS/time-of-day distribution (e.g., 9–11am peak 45% of daily traffic) and how many concurrent long-lived streams (if any)?
3) Any must-have compliance controls that would rule out hosted multi-tenant (e.g., no multi-tenant processing of tokens)?

Suggested next steps:
- You share the request distribution and any sample logs (anonymized).
- We run a two-week dedicated pilot for the checkout path (reserved capacity) to validate the P95 target and isolate worst-case tails.
- Simultaneously run a 2-week Hosted canary for non-real-time endpoints to measure economics and fallbacks.
- Deliverable: performance report + cost delta and a recommendation (Hosted/Dedicated/mixed).

Attaching a quick matrix I promised (post-demo-matrix.xlsx). If you prefer, we can run a short synthetic pilot first.

Timing: We can start kickoff next week (w/c Apr 17) if the anonymized traffic sample is available by EOD Mon.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Ben/Tessa on sizing.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0173

Attachment: post-demo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet with endpoints, p95 goals, rough QPS breakdown)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@streamlinepay.com>

Cc: Priya Desai <priya@streamlinepay.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting path probe & latency/throughput clarifications

Karthik — thanks for the clean recap. Short answers below and a bit more color from our side.

1) Checkout P95: this is a hard UX requirement for the checkout surface — marketing and ops have zero tolerance over 100ms during checkout; 80ms is our internal goal.
2) Traffic distribution: peak 9–11am (about 40% of daily volume), secondary spike 7–9pm (20%). Typical sustained QPS 15–25 rps across the whole stack, but checkout is spiky and short-lived (concurrent spikes up to 600, spikes to 900 during promos). I can paste an anonymized log sample as CSV.
3) Compliance: we do not want multi-tenant processing of payment tokens. We are OK with a managed environment if it provides tenant isolation (VPC or dedicated pool) and HSM/KMS integration; SOC2 is required.

Pilot preference: ideally we'd avoid heavy infra ownership. If Dedicated reserved capacity can give the isolation and an SLA we can sign off on, that's appealing for checkout. For other endpoints we are more cost-sensitive and open to Hosted if the economics are right.

Ask: can you provide a rough cost delta (order-of-magnitude) between Dedicated reserved for checkout vs. Hosted with guaranteed fallback? Also please include an estimate for required GPU type assuming a 7B-style model with half-precision quantization.

Thanks — attaching a small sample anonymized traffic CSV in the next email.

—
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering | StreamlinePay
sanjay@streamlinepay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting path probe & latency/throughput clarifications

Quick internal note — Sanjay's numbers point strongly to a hybrid approach. A few points: 

- Checkout: dedicated reserved capacity (1–2 GPU nodes, depending on model memory/seq) gives deterministic tail latency and avoids multi-tenant processing of tokens. With a 7B model quantized, we expect a single A100-style slice or equivalent Ampere-class instance to handle ~500–700 concurrent short requests with optimized batching; so plan conservatively for 2 nodes for headroom.
- Non-real-time endpoints: Hosted looks attractive — lower management overhead and cheaper at scale if latency budget is relaxed.
- Cost delta: rough ballpark for 2-node Dedicated reserved (monthly amortized) vs Hosted on-demand serving for similar QPS is ~2.5–3x more expensive for Dedicated at steady-state, but Dedicated will deliver 2–4x better P95 tail behavior under burst. We'll formalize numbers once we see sample logs.

Proposed pilot plan (high level):
1) Two-week Dedicated reserved pilot for checkout (isolation + SLA testing). Include KMS/HSM integration and limited ingress rules.
2) Two-week Hosted canary for other endpoints to compare unit economics.

I'll draft an initial pilot plan and cost estimate; attaching initial-pilot-plan.pdf and a quick hosting-cost-estimate.csv (rough multipliers). We should offer Sanjay a single point-of-contact for the pilot (ops+solutions).

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Director | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting path probe & latency/throughput clarifications

Sanjay — thanks for the sample data. Based on your numbers and Ben's sizing note, here's a concrete pilot proposal and proposed timeline so we can move to an SOW quickly if this looks right.

Pilot proposal (recommended hybrid):
- Checkout (latency-critical): Dedicated reserved pool (2 nodes) with tenant isolation, KMS integration for token handling, and SLA measurements. Duration: 2 weeks (performance validation + degradation testing).
- Non-critical endpoints: Hosted canary for 2 weeks (measure economics and failover behavior).

What we will deliver:
- Performance report (P95 / P99 / tail latencies) per endpoint with real traffic and synthetic worst-case spikes.
- Cost comparison: Dedicated reserved amortized vs Hosted consumption for the observed traffic profile.
- Security audit checklist: confirmation of SOC2 controls and KMS integration notes.

Timeline:
- Kickoff: week of Apr 17 (requires anonymized logs by EOD Mon).
- Dedicated provisioning & KMS setup: 3 business days from kickoff.
- Run pilot: 2 weeks (we'll capture rolling performance and a final analysis).
- Delivery: pilot report within 5 business days after pilot ends.

Next asks from you to proceed: anonymized traffic CSV (thanks for prepping), sign-off on pilot dates, and a rough list of the endpoints you want in Dedicated vs Hosted.

I'll put together the formal SOW and a more detailed cost delta (we'll show per-100k requests unit economics) and share HubSpot record HS-8931 and a Drive folder with the pilot artifacts.

Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1xA_streamlinepay-pilot-matrix | HubSpot: HS-8931

If that plan looks good, I'll follow up with a calendar invite and a short SOW draft.

—
